headline: Federal government will hold about 721 acres in San Diego County in trust for the Pala Band of Mission Indians.
what_it_does: The law directs the Department of the Interior to take about 721.12 acres of land in San Diego County, California, into trust for the Pala Band of Mission Indians. This happens if the tribe transfers the land's title to the United States. The land becomes part of the Pala Indian Reservation. Gaming is generally not allowed on this land.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the Pala Band of Mission Indians
who_it_affects.how: Their tribe's reservation grows by about 721 acres held in trust by the federal government.
It must take the land into trust once the tribe transfers the title to the United States.
Gaming is generally banned on the land added to the reservation.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted July 28, 2023; the land is taken into trust once the tribe transfers title to the United States.
